previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and HIV presented with chills, pain, and purulent drainage from her right femoral tunneled dialysis catheter, concerning for infection. She also reported new vaginal discharge and lower abdominal pain. Blood cultures were negative, but the catheter tip grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), confirming infection. The infected catheter was removed and replaced with a new left femoral tunneled catheter. She was treated with a four-week course of vancomycin administered during dialysis. A venogram revealed IVC stenosis, which was partially treated with balloon plasty. Vaginal swabs were negative for infections, and symptoms were managed with a single dose of fluconazole. Her HIV was managed with continued antiretroviral therapy, and her low CD4 count was noted. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue antibiotics, resume midodrine for dialysis-related hypotension, and follow up with her PCP, dermatology, and vascular surgery.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
